title: Terminal Ledger — Bloomberg Floor Dispatch
description: A trading-floor briefing slide built around a dense monospaced data table, live-ticker header bar, and fixed commentary panel — differentiated by its unapologetic terminal-UI discipline and zero-ornament information hierarchy.
philosophy: This template exists because financial data professionals are poorly served by slides that prioritize beauty over bandwidth. Modelled on Bloomberg terminal conventions and physical trading-floor display boards, it treats every pixel as a data carrier and refuses gradients, illustration, and decorative whitespace on principle. The monospaced grid is the design; breaking it is the only mistake a presenter can make. It is built for an audience that reads tables faster than paragraphs and trusts density as a signal of rigor.
goodFor: Internal trading-desk morning briefings with multi-row ticker data
Risk management snapshots requiring dense tabular position summaries
Quant or algo team reviews where column-aligned numbers are read at speed
Live market-status update slides with timestamped header bars
avoidFor: Client-facing pitch decks requiring brand polish or visual warmth
Executive narrative slides needing breathing room and large type
Presentations to non-specialist audiences unfamiliar with terminal-style layouts
Any context requiring imagery, illustration, or chart-first storytelling
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a trading terminal snapping to attention at market open — institutional, unornamented, and carrying low-frequency urgency beneath its stillness. Compositional rhythm is rigid and left-anchored, machine-legible label-value pairs substituting for any conventional hero typography. The mood should read as a system identifier, not a designed cover: authority through density, not through graphic gesture. Avoid all softness, curvature, decorative spacing, or visual warmth — any tension present must come from structured information pressing against a hard grid.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-width ticker-bar strip runs edge-to-edge at the top (~10% of canvas height), carrying session metadata in a single scrolling row. Title block is left-anchored in cols 1–8 of a 12-col monospaced grid, vertically centered in the remaining canvas with a tight fixed-gutter rail — no outer breathing margin. A secondary status block (deck ID, timestamp, desk designation) occupies cols 9–12 bottom-right as a flush column of label-value pairs. Hierarchy is enforced entirely through label prefixes (e.g., 'SESSION:', 'BRIEFING:') and character-width contrast, never through size scaling.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a terminal pulled from a trading desk: relentless column alignment, every element either a number or a label. Mood is cold-room rigor — authoritative, fluorescent, zero ambiguity. Compositional rhythm is dense-modular: the table breathes only through ruled lines rather than whitespace, while the commentary panel acts as a narrow annotation strip rather than narrative prose. Avoid anything that softens the grid — no rounded corners, no icons, no decorative separators.
